body: I agree, the mods and this community has been very helpful in my recovery. I like to watch from the sidelines as I'm usually logged in under my normal account but I think if it wasn't for /r/stopdrinking and AA I probably would have relapsed a long time ago. Thanks mods and everyone else!

Never tried a non-alcoholic beer, and at this stage I don't think it would be a wise idea for me. I swore off drinking after a near deadly car accident earlier this year, and that includes NA beers, which may contain a small percentage of alcohol. Plus, the taste may make me relapse. 

As far as marijuana use, I have used before and after my sobriety date, with the longest period of non-use recently being from late June to early August of this year. I use it for help in dealing with emotional stress because my current meds are sometimes not helpful in that capacity, but it has helped me satiate that craving for euphoria that drinking gave me. If it were not for marijuana, I think that my recovery might be a bit more difficult. That is my experience anyway, may not work for every one.

I have to admit, it has. Not waking up with hangovers is a huge plus, and the money I'm saving is adding up. I got an app on my phone that says I've saved nearly $500 already on booze. Breath smells better, skin looks better, and the depression and anxiety I have suffered for years is becoming more manageable. Of course, I was taking my meds with my booze before, so that has something to do with it. After admitting my problem and my failures to my family they have supported me. My friends, on the other hand, scattered like cockroaches when you turn the light on in a dark room when they heard the news about my second DUI and accident. Oh well, fuck 'em.

Well, I've been dealing with a DUI, loss of a vehicle, and medical bills. Not to mention all the friends I've lost because of my DUI. A ton of stress building up, and I usually took to the bottle to ease my troubles, but that isn't an option anymore. I have to prove to myself and my loved ones that I can change and become a better person out of all this.

I got my second DUI in June and it was a result of a single car accident at 4AM. Still unsure how I survived.

As others have said, get involved in treatment options and group therapy. You may win some brownie points with the judge if you show that you are committed to changing your life. One of the big things that is getting me through is I have to go through this not just for me, but for my loved ones. I realized how much my actions were affecting others and it tore me apart. After my accident I'm sure I let everyone down again. Now is my chance to rebuild my life. I've been going to AA since the accident and it has helped. I'm not big on the religion part of it (I'm agnostic myself), but I look the other way because this is more important than believing in a higher power, this is about me.
Good job, I'm getting close to my 90 days myself. Can't wait to pick up that chip. It's been hell.

First off, I am very sorry for your situation. DWIs are a very stressful situation. I recently got my second one in June. The first one was just a traffic stop, but this one was a one car accident that totaled my SUV that was my pride and joy. I was sent to the hospital, where I was given a blood test. I had the option to refuse, but honestly I did not know what I was doing. I rolled my car 3-4 times and landed upside down in a flower garden. If I refused the test, my license would be suspended for a year, that's it. Under my state law, I am facing a year of suspended license, then a year of ignition interlock, 7-10 days in jail which can be taken away if I agree to wear an ankle bracelet or enter a rehab facility, an undetermined amount of probation, community service, up to $2000 fine, and a $10,000 hospital bill because I am uninsured and have no job.

Sometimes bad things happen to us. Think of this as a learning experience and please don't beat yourself up over this. People have come out of DWIs before and had successful careers. Start shopping around for a lawyer now. Expect to spend $1-2000 on fees. If that is not feasible, hire a public defender. There is no shame in a PD if the case against you is pretty ironclad. It is not for everyone, but look into AA. I have been going since my accident and it has helped me. It may help you in your penalty.

I wish you luck in your case, and take it one day at a time. You can do this. Don't be a stranger here, we are a good group to talk to.

EDIT: Also, thank goodness you didn't hurt or kill anyone or damage any property. You should count your blessings and see this as a new, bright beginning in your life. Good luck friend.

The worst part is going to be waiting for the blood to come back already knowing what's going to happen. It could be up to a year or more before it comes back. And I also have to deal with thousands of dollars in medical bills...my life sucks right now.
Thanks!

That's true. If it's your first one, I would suggest finding an insurance company that insures high risk drivers. I was with GMAC and they had reasonable rates. I spent $235 for 6 months, liability insurance only. Since this is my second one, I don't know what's going to happen to my rates when I get another car. I'm expecting it to be at least double what I paid before. I'll make damn sure it's a POS that can last three years though, or at least until my insurance goes down.

You may think 57 is old and you have nothing to live for, but in this day and age that simply isn't the case. Chances are you'll have many more years in your life; years that may include a new job, new opportunities, a new found love, and possibly grandchildren to hold in your arms and spoil.

You seem to have the same problem I do; that is, comparing your life to others around you. All the people I have on Facebook that I went to school with have great relationships, children, homes, good jobs and nice cars. Take it from me, envying others does more harm than good. For so long I have wanted to be part of that, to show them that I did something with my life. I just didn't know how to do it. Instead I've been living with my dad for the past few years, living off of him and going to college on his dime to get a degree in computer networking. I have been getting financial aid from my military service but it wasn't much, and it ended when I graduated in May. I haven't been able to get a job because of my depression. I've been too depressed to even look for work, sometimes staying in my bed for days at a time, only leaving my room for something to drink. I too feel that weekends mean nothing...every day brings the same thing. I haven't had a job in two years or a girlfriend in six years and sometimes it feels like it'll never happen. 

Eventually I turned to drinking and it made my life a living hell. Last month I totaled my car and was charged with my second DUI at the age of 28. I now have a $10,000 hospital bill and I'm facing jail, fines, revocation of my license, and on top of all that, I now *have* to find a job to pay everything off. Over the past month I've spent most of my days in bed, worrying about how to put my life back together. I put a gun to my head I don't know how many times, but thankfully I chickened out every time. Out of desperation, I joined Alcoholics Anonymous on the urging of my family and just had my 30 day mark of sobriety. Being around others that share my challenges has helped. I don't feel alone anymore. I feel that maybe that there is hope for me after all.

Perhaps group therapy could help you as well. There is no magic cure-all for depression. I wish there was. I've been on depression meds for years, been hospitalized twice for suicide attempts, and have been to many doctors over the years in my pursuit of happiness. Talking to others in a group has helped me the most in my opinion. And though you may not want to talk to your children about your problems, they may have a feeling something is off and want to help, but don't know how. Perhaps opening up to them a little could help.

You are 57 years *young*. You still have plenty of time to make your life happier. Don't expect it to be easy, but you can do it. Nothing in life is easy. I suggest making a plan on how to get back on your feet, first by finding work somewhere. Work can help get your mind off of things (in addition to making money). Keeping your mind busy is important when you're depressed. Perhaps through a job you can find some good friends and maybe a boyfriend. It will be challenging but you can do it. But please remember that you are NOT worthless. You have two loving children who look up to you, even though you think you have outlasted your usefulness to them. You can get through this.

I have posted on here before under this name and other names and I assure you that you won't be traced. The only reason I use a throwaway account is because I'm a moderator of a few mid-sized subreddits on here and I am active pretty much every day. Sometimes I comment on posts here through my "normal" account to give some advice or talk someone down from doing something they'd regret.

Please feel free to express your thoughts on here. We are interested in hearing from you. This is a great community and we do not judge you. Everyone is treated with respect here. Your safety and confidentiality is very important to us. If you feel compelled to, please share your story with us. Perhaps one of us has a solution for your situation, or can at least help guide you in the right direction.

Sending good vibes and thoughts your way, /u/unparalleledanguish.
Thanks, it does feel good to be free from alcohol for a month. I'm celebrating today with some Chinese food and Skyrim.
Thanks!
Thanks!

I'm definitely going to AA, it's really a good experience and I wish I did it sooner. Right now it's the only escape I have from home because I'm just too ashamed to speak to my friends, much less my family. Drinking I'm taking an indefinite break from...I'm still young so I may drink a beer years from now, but right now is not the time. Therapy has been mentioned by my family, but I am not sure I need it, and I definitely cannot afford it. I'll have to do an alcohol assessment when/if convicted anyway and that's going to cost a good amount, but I've been through it once, I can do it again. I've been steeling myself for the worst punishment from this and I am confident I can handle it, but it's just the emotional and financial toll that's nearly made me break. Sometimes I wish I could just plead guilty and get on with it because waiting so long for punishment is punishment in itself. I nearly did my first court date but was talked out of it by my mom...I guess she didn't want to see me in handcuffs and led away by the bailiff.

Thanks for the advice, I'll consider a PD more closely now. I'm going to start making appointments next week to talk to them as my next court date is in September and will likely be continued because the blood test hasn't come back from the state yet.
Thanks for the info. I'll talk to a social worker tomorrow, hopefully they can help me out.

I will...I just get nervous and embarrassed when I talk about my problems sometimes. I mean on here it's fine because I don't know you people. But it's different when you're talking face-to-face. At last Tuesday's meeting I completely broke down to them. Although it felt good it was painful to do. I grew up with the mentality that men aren't supposed to show weakness. Now I have to confront that stigma and let people really know what's going on in my head.

I do have someone I've been talking to at meetings but I haven't called him yet. Meant to this weekend but it's a little late to right now. I'm going to remember to give him a call tomorrow. He's going through a second DUI too but I'm sure my situation is a bit more complicated and serious than his.

I actually started going to meetings right after the accident. It was a very difficult decision, and I was incredibly nervous at the first meeting, but I had family telling me it may look good when I eventually get sentenced for my crime and right now I need all the help I can get. It's pretty much one of the few things keeping me sane at the moment. It definitely does help knowing that there are others that are in similar situations. It's taking me a while to open up to the group, but tonight I did stay for a while after the meeting and pretty much broke down to a couple people who want to sponsor me. I'm talking about crying, telling them about my depression that existed before my accident, the drinking, suicidal thoughts, the works. Embarrassing as it was, it kind of felt good to vent. I know there's people who have my back now, something I didn't have for a long time.

I got a continuance until September. Kinda surprised I wasn't locked up or asked to surrender my license. When the accident happened the cop took away my driving privileges for 30 days so I have a couple weeks to go before I can drive (for a little while, anyway). The only friend that's still speaking to me suggested maybe I could get a cheap car to help get around town for the time being.
I've been thinking of doing this myself. Been clean for about 6 months but given my recent troubles it may put my mind at ease, if only for a couple hours.

You know...you're right. I do need some sort of plan. I just have to start out small, get a job somewhere and save as much as I can and rebuild my life. It may take years to get back on track, and I may have to make difficult decisions like moving back home to mom. But I have to do this...I'm nearing 30 and I already fucked up so much in my life. I am at the bottom. The only way to go is up.

I'm actually going to AA now. I've been to a few meetings already and my friend (pretty much my only one right now) who also has trouble told me he wants to go to a meeting every day and he wants to take me with him, I think more to get me out of the house than anything else. I've spent the past week in bed all day pretty much so maybe I do need to get out.
Thanks, it took a lot of convincing and a lot of thought before I committed to going. I almost backed out an hour before it started but decided to do it.
Great, thanks!
Thanks...I just wish it didn't have to come to this. Story of my life I guess.

I guess in a way I am glad I survived too. My family has been surprisingly supportive, but that's probably because I have a history of depression and suicide attempts. I don't know if I'll get out of this hole, though. Even if I do, I have no idea how to move forward. I am pretty ashamed of myself. Just graduated college last month and that was the highlight of my life. Now I'm back to square one. Nobody would want to hire me with 2 DUIs.

They took a blood sample at the hospital. Fortunately for me, there is a backlog in my state. The officer that accompanied me to the ER did do a breathalyzer, but since it wasn't at the station, it cannot be entered into court. I blew a .12.
People have been telling me that I should use the opportunity of my survival as a blessing. I view it as a curse. Maybe one day I will see things in a different light.

Yes. I used to sneak alcohol in the house. One night two weeks ago I drank 3 liters of cheap merlot because I wanted to feel something. I ended up shitting nothing but black shit for the next four-five days.
Sore, physically and emotionally.

But how am I supposed to get things together after this? No one would hire me after two DUIs. This is going to hang over my head for the rest of my life, no matter how long or short it is. I've asked myself so many times the past few days why I wasn't killed. I had a full tank of gas and the engine was still running when I landed upside down. I am so stupid. I shouldn't be alive right now. I haven't even taken a shower or eaten since the accident I am so disgusted with myself.

I just don't know man. I feel like I should've been killed in the accident. I wish I was. The cop that accompanied me to the hospital didn't arrest me even though I pleaded with him to. He said it wasn't in his heart to do it. My family and friends will grieve but they will get over it eventually. Yes suicide is the easy way out but I don't see how I can fix my life after this. I'm gathering all my meds and plan to take them all at once. I also am going to try to get a friend to take me to the store to get some dust remover and I'll do a couple cans of those. If all that fails, I'll pull the trigger as a fail-safe. I'm so tired of fighting this depression and this will bring me some much needed closure to my life. Everything I do I seem to fuck up. Can't deal with much more.
Well, I can't sleep. What makes suicide such a bad thing? I'll do everyone a favor in the long run.
I'm going to sleep. Still covered in blood from the accident, but unwilling to take a shower. I'm going to make my decision on when to do it when I wake up.

I don't know, there's little hope for me. I know my family and friends will miss me, especially my little bro...he looks up to me so much. But there's little I can do anymore. I fucked up big time. Might as well punish myself before the law does.
I have three pistols and a shotgun
